is_transient.instructions: Given the job metadata and the last 200 log lines in state.job / state.log_tail, does the failure look like a transient condition (network blip, DNS/registry timeout, runner provisioning error, disk/rate-limit contention, flaky test known to be order- or timing-dependent) rather than a deterministic problem with the code or configuration under test?

criteria.true: The log shows infra/network/environment symptoms (timeouts, connection resets, registry/DNS failures, OOM-killed runner, docker pull errors, rate limiting) with no indication the actual code logic is wrong.
criteria.false: The log shows a deterministic failure caused by the code/config itself (compile error, failed assertion, type error, lint failure, missing file committed, bad config) that will reproduce on an identical retry.

failure_category.instructions: Classify the root cause of this CI job failure using state.job and state.log_tail.

criteria.infra_flake: CI infrastructure/network issue: registry/DNS timeout, runner provisioning failure, docker pull error, rate limiting, disk full on runner.
criteria.test_flake: A test failed in a way consistent with known flakiness: timing/race condition, order-dependent test, nondeterministic external service in a unit test, intermittent timeout in an otherwise-passing suite.
criteria.code_defect: A real bug: failed assertion tied to the code change, exception from application logic, type/compile error.
criteria.dependency_or_config: Build/config problem: missing dependency, bad lockfile, misconfigured env var/secret, broken CI config.
criteria.unknown: Log is inconclusive or truncated; cannot confidently attribute a cause.

retry_value.instructions: Considering state.job.attempt vs state.job.maxAttempts and the nature of the failure in state.log_tail, how much expected value is there in retrying this job (likelihood a retry succeeds, weighed against wasted compute if it will just fail again the same way)?
